# `android` operations

32 operations. Generated from `assets/operations.json`; [all references](index.md).

### android.screen

Android screen preview. writes, idempotent.

Save an Android device's screen as a PNG at path at once, through adb exec-out screencap, within 10 seconds and without a job, for previews that refresh such as the desktop's device grid. The result has the file's size and the picture's width and height. For evidence kept with a job, use device.capture.

- `device` string, required (non-empty): Device serial / UDID from device.list
- `path` string, required (non-empty): Absolute path of the PNG to write; an existing file is replaced.

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.screen '{"device":"<device>","path":"<path>"}'
```

### android.store_screenshots

Capture store screenshots. writes.

Capture store screenshots of an installed Android app as a job: on each device, for each app language (set with android.settings app_locale, Android 13 and newer) and each of light and dark mode, every screen in order: stop and launch the app, run the screen's testing.run steps, wait settle_ms and save the screen. Files go to DIRECTORY/THEME/LOCALE/images/KIND/NN_SCREEN.png, where KIND is phoneScreenshots, sevenInchScreenshots or tenInchScreenshots by the device's smallest width, so each THEME folder is a fastlane supply metadata directory. Animations are off while capturing; each device's dark mode, animations and app language are put back afterwards. report.json lists every file with its size and play_problems (a side under 320 or over 3840 pixels, or longer than 2:1).

- `bundle_id` string, required (non-empty): Application ID of the installed app
- `devices` array of string, required (1 to 8 items): Serials from device.list, at most one per screen size group
- `locales` array of string, required (1 to 30 items): App languages as Google Play's language codes, such as en-US or de-DE
- `screens` array of object {name, steps}, required (1 to 10 items): Screens in store order
- `directory` string, required (non-empty): Absolute path of an empty or new directory for the screenshots
- `themes` array of string (items one of light, dark; 1 to 2 items): Defaults to light only
- `settle_ms` integer (0 to 30000; default 1000): Wait after the last step before capturing
- `timeout` integer (10 to 86400; default 3600): Seconds for the whole job

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.store_screenshots '{"bundle_id":"<bundle_id>","devices":["<device>"],"locales":["<locale>"],"screens":[{"name":"<name>"}],"directory":"<directory>"}'
```

### android.input

Tap / swipe / input. writes.

Control real Android UI through adb, using device pixel coordinates. ASCII text is typed; other text is pasted through the device clipboard with the configured scrcpy 4.1 server on Android 7 and newer.

- `device` string, required (non-empty): Device serial / UDID from device.list
- `action` string, required (one of tap, swipe, text, keyevent)
- `x` integer (0 to 16384; default 0)
- `y` integer (0 to 16384; default 0)
- `end_x` integer (0 to 16384; default 0)
- `end_y` integer (0 to 16384; default 0)
- `duration` integer (1 to 10000; default 300)
- `text` string (default "")
- `key` string (default "KEYCODE_HOME")

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.input '{"device":"<device>","action":"tap"}'
```

### android.settings

Device settings for tests. writes, idempotent.

Read or set what changes an app's look and motion in UI tests and screenshots: dark mode, font scale, animations, airplane mode and one app's language. Arguments left out stay as they are; the result reads every setting back and reports a value Android did not apply as setting_not_applied.

- `device` string, required (non-empty): Device serial / UDID from device.list
- `dark_mode` string (one of on, off, auto): System dark theme; auto follows the device schedule
- `font_scale` number (0.5 to 2): System font size; 1 is the default
- `animations` boolean: false sets the window, transition and animator scales to 0; true sets them to 1
- `airplane_mode` boolean: Android 11 and newer
- `bundle_id` string: App whose language app_locale sets and the result reads
- `app_locale` string: Language tags separated by commas, such as de-DE or fr,en; empty follows the device language again. Android 13 and newer.

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.settings '{"device":"<device>"}'
```

### android.display

Display orientation and size. writes, idempotent.

Lock the screen orientation, override the display size or density, or reset them, on a phone or emulator; the result reads all three back. A value Android did not apply answers setting_not_applied. With no other argument it only reads.

- `device` string, required (non-empty): Device serial / UDID from device.list
- `orientation` string (one of auto, portrait, landscape, reverse-portrait, reverse-landscape): Lock the rotation; auto follows the sensor again
- `width` integer (100 to 10000): Override width in pixels, with height
- `height` integer (100 to 10000): Override height in pixels, with width
- `density` integer (72 to 1000): Override density in dpi
- `reset` boolean (default false): Return size and density to the device's own and rotation to the sensor, before anything else given

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.display '{"device":"<device>"}'
```

### android.notifications

Notifications. writes.

List the notifications Android is showing, with key, package, title, text, channel and flags; open or close the notification shade; or snooze one notification by its key. Every action returns the list afterwards. adb cannot cancel another app's notifications, so snooze hides one for a time instead.

- `device` string, required (non-empty): Device serial / UDID from device.list
- `action` string (one of list, open, close, snooze; default "list"): open and close expand or collapse the notification shade
- `bundle_id` string: List only this app's notifications
- `key` string: Notification key from the list, for snooze
- `seconds` integer (1 to 604800; default 3600): How long snooze hides the notification

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.notifications '{"device":"<device>"}'
```

### android.app_files

App data files. writes.

List or pull the private files of a debuggable app (its data directory, through run-as). pull returns a job that writes the files as one .tar archive. Release builds answer app_not_debuggable. To clear app data or force-stop the app, use device.app.

- `device` string, required (non-empty): Device serial / UDID from device.list
- `bundle_id` string, required: Application ID of a debuggable build
- `action` string (one of list, pull; default "list")
- `path` string (default "."): File or directory inside the app's data directory, relative to it, such as files or databases/app.db
- `output` string (default ""): Absolute local path of the .tar archive, for pull

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.app_files '{"device":"<device>","bundle_id":"<bundle_id>"}'
```

### android.each

Run on every Android device. **destructive, ask first**.

Run the same steps on every connected Android device, or on the listed ones, as one job: all devices at once, each device's steps in order until one fails. A step that returns a job is followed to its end. The job's report.json artifact has every device's result; the job fails if any device failed. Steps leave out device and platform, which are set per device.

- `steps` array of object {operation, arguments}, required (1 to 20 items)
- `devices` array of string (up to 100 items): Serials from device.list; all online Android devices when left out
- `timeout` integer (10 to 86400; default 1800): Seconds for the whole job

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.each '{"steps":[{"operation":"device.install"}]}'
```

### android.pair

Pair over Wi-Fi by QR code. writes.

Wireless debugging pairing by QR code, for Android 11 and newer. action qr makes a one-time service name and password and returns the QR code the phone's Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with QR code scans: qr_text, the modules as qr.rows (1 is dark), an SVG, and with path a PNG or SVG file. Nothing is stored. action wait, with that service and password, waits up to timeout seconds for the phone to offer the code on the local network (adb mdns), pairs with adb pair and connects to the phone's debugging service; the result names the device to use. Call wait again while the code shows; pairing_timeout means the phone has not scanned it yet. action services lists what adb finds on the network, such as the address the phone shows under Pair device with pairing code, for android.connect with pairing_code.

- `action` string (one of qr, wait, services; default "qr"): qr shows a new code, wait pairs once the phone scanned it, services lists discovered devices.
- `service` string: For wait: the service name action qr returned.
- `password` string: For wait: the password action qr returned.
- `timeout` integer (1 to 300; default 60): For wait: how many seconds to wait for the phone.
- `path` string (default ""): For qr: an absolute path ending in .png or .svg to write the code to.

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.pair
```

### android.avd_configure

Set emulator performance. writes, idempotent.

Persist graphics, RAM and CPU settings for a stopped registered Android emulator. Preserves app data and other configuration, saves the original configuration, and skips incompatible VM snapshots on subsequent Tomacco starts. Running AVDs are rejected.

- `name` string, required
- `gpu` string (one of auto, host, software, swiftshader, lavapipe)
- `memory_mb` integer (512 to 32768)
- `cores` integer (1 to 32)
- `vulkan` string (one of auto, on, off): Vulkan compatibility override; off keeps OpenGL ES and avoids the Vulkan interoperability path. Requires a cold restart.

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.avd_configure '{"name":"<name>"}'
```

### android.avd_start

Start emulator. writes, idempotent.

Start or reuse an Android virtual device. A Tomacco-managed AVD resumes from its Quick Boot snapshot when android.emulator saved one at its last stop; the result's boot says quick or cold and why. CPU acceleration remains enabled independently of the selected GPU renderer. A start with a window needs X11 (DISPLAY, XWayland on Wayland) and is refused with emulator_no_display without it; the emulator gets QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb when the session names only wayland. With gpu configured and the AVD's default auto renderer, a host without a hardware GPU driver starts with swiftshader (gpu in the result says so).

- `name` string, required
- `headless` boolean (default false)
- `software` boolean (default false)
- `gpu` string (one of configured, auto, host, software, swiftshader, lavapipe; default "configured"): configured respects the saved AVD renderer; auto selects a compatible renderer; host uses the computer GPU. An override applies to this start. Changing…
- `cold_boot` boolean (default false): Boot fully instead of loading the Quick Boot snapshot, for example after changing the GPU renderer. App data is retained.
- `audio` boolean (default true): Enable the emulator host audio backend independently of headless mode. Embedded clients can disable this and use runtime.audio instead. Applied only to a new…
- `vulkan` string (one of configured, auto, on, off; default "configured"): Vulkan compatibility override; off keeps OpenGL ES and avoids the Vulkan interoperability path. Requires a cold restart.
- `camera_image` string (non-empty): Absolute path of a PNG or JPEG the emulated camera shows instead of its scene, for QR code and document scanning. Applied only to a new emulator process, which…
- `camera_facing` string (one of back, front; default "back"): Which camera shows camera_image

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.avd_start '{"name":"<name>"}'
```

### android.emulator

Control emulator. **destructive, ask first**.

Stop an emulator, saving the Quick Boot snapshot of a Tomacco-managed one so its next start resumes in seconds; save, load, list or delete its snapshots; set its GPS location, battery or network speed and latency through the emulator console. A command the console refuses answers emulator_refused.

- `device` string, required (non-empty): Device serial / UDID from device.list
- `action` string, required (one of stop, snapshot-save, snapshot-load, snapshot-list, snapshot-delete, location, battery, network)
- `name` string (default "default"): Snapshot name for snapshot-save, snapshot-load and snapshot-delete
- `longitude` number (-180 to 180; default 0)
- `latitude` number (-90 to 90; default 0)
- `battery_level` integer (0 to 100; default 100): Battery charge in percent, for battery
- `charging` boolean (default true): Whether the charger is connected, for battery
- `network_speed` string (one of gsm, hscsd, gprs, edge, umts, hsdpa, lte, evdo, 5g, full; default "full"): Network speed preset, for network; full means no limit
- `network_delay` string (one of gprs, edge, umts, none; default "none"): Network latency, for network: gprs 150-550 ms, edge 80-400 ms, umts 35-200 ms, none adds no latency
- `save_quick_boot` boolean (default true): For stop: save the Quick Boot snapshot of a Tomacco-managed emulator first, which its next android.avd_start loads. Other emulators are never saved.

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.emulator '{"device":"<device>","action":"stop"}'
```

### android.package_inspect

Inspect APK or AAB. read-only, idempotent.

Read an APK or AAB without a device: package, version name and code, minimum, target and compile SDK, permissions, native ABIs and signing certificates with their SHA-256 digests. APKs go through aapt2 and apksigner from the SDK build-tools; an AAB's manifest is read directly and its signature through keytool. Reads the file only.

- `path` string, required (non-empty): Absolute path of an .apk or .aab file

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.package_inspect '{"path":"<path>"}'
```

### android.size_report

Report APK or AAB size. read-only, idempotent.

Break an APK or AAB down by size without a device: totals, each category (dex, native, resources, assets, manifest, signature), each ABI, screen density and bundle module, and the largest files. estimate.by_abi_density adds up the compressed sizes one device would get without other ABIs' libraries and other densities' resources. For an AAB with bundletool configured, download has bundletool get-size total's download size per ABI and density, from APKs it builds in a temporary directory. baseline compares with an earlier build: the change of every total and the files that grew, shrank, appeared or went away the most.

- `path` string, required (non-empty): Absolute path of an .apk or .aab file
- `baseline` string (default ""): Absolute path of an earlier .apk or .aab to compare with
- `top` integer (1 to 200; default 15): How many of the largest and most changed files to list
- `bundletool` boolean (default true): For an AAB, also ask bundletool for the download size; false reads the file only

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.size_report '{"path":"<path>"}'
```

### android.sensors

Emulator sensors. writes.

Simulate the sensors of an Android emulator through its console. status lists every sensor with its values; set gives one sensor values; orientation turns the device by gravity and reads back the display rotation Android chose; shake shakes the accelerometer for about a second; proximity covers or uncovers the proximity sensor; light sets the ambient light; fingerprint touches the fingerprint sensor with an enrolled finger, for a biometric prompt; posture folds, half-opens or opens a foldable emulator.

- `device` string, required (non-empty): Emulator serial from device.list, such as emulator-5554
- `action` string, required (one of status, set, orientation, shake, proximity, light, fingerprint, posture)
- `sensor` string (non-empty): For set: a sensor name from status, such as acceleration or magnetic-field
- `values` array of number (1 to 6 items): For set: the sensor's values, such as x, y and z
- `orientation` string (one of portrait, landscape, reverse-portrait, reverse-landscape; default "portrait"): For orientation: how the device is held
- `near` boolean (default true): For proximity: whether something covers the sensor
- `lux` number (0 to 100000; default 300): For light: ambient light in lux
- `finger_id` integer (1 to 10; default 1): For fingerprint: the enrolled finger, as the emulator numbers them
- `posture` string (one of closed, half-open, open; default "open"): For posture: the foldable's hinge

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.sensors '{"device":"<device>","action":"status"}'
```

### android.app_links

App Links. writes.

Check an app's Android App Links. status reads each web domain the app declares with autoVerify and its verification state (verified, none, denied, or the verifier's error code) and the user's link choices; verify asks Android to verify the domains again and waits up to seconds for the answers, which need the domains' assetlinks.json and a network; resolve names the app and activity a link opens, or that Android shows a chooser, and every app that could open it; set approves, denies or resets domains by hand, as tests of a debug build need. Opening a link is android.deep_link.

- `device` string, required (non-empty): Device serial / UDID from device.list
- `action` string (one of status, verify, resolve, set; default "status")
- `bundle_id` string (non-empty): The app's application ID; for resolve it adds opens_in_app
- `url` string (non-empty): For resolve: the link, such as https://example.com/item/1
- `seconds` integer (0 to 120; default 30): For verify: how long to wait for the verifier
- `state` string (one of approved, denied, none; default "approved"): For set: the state to give the domains
- `domains` array of string: For set: domains the app declares; all of them when left out

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.app_links '{"device":"<device>"}'
```

### android.network_capture

Network capture. writes.

Capture the network traffic of an emulator, or only what one app sends, and summarise it: hosts with bytes and connections, TLS server names, HTTP requests with method, host and path but no query, and DNS queries. Contents are never in the summary; HTTPS stays encrypted, as no certificate is installed. start needs opt_in:true, a running emulator whose image allows root through su (Google APIs or AOSP, not Google Play) and runs the image's tcpdump; bundle_id limits it to the app's outgoing packets through an iptables rule that stop removes. stop ends it, copies the pcap file, readable only by you, to path and summarises it; summary reads any pcap file.

- `action` string, required (one of start, stop, summary)
- `device` string (non-empty): Emulator serial from device.list, such as emulator-5554
- `opt_in` boolean (default false): For start: confirm that every packet, contents included, may be recorded
- `bundle_id` string (non-empty): For start: capture only what this app sends
- `path` string (non-empty): For stop: where to write the pcap file, absolute; by default under Tomacco's data. For summary: the pcap file to read

```sh
tomaccoctl call android.network_capture '{"action":"start"}'
```
